tone_statements.citation: Bird, Steven. 1999. Strategies for representing tone in African writing systems. Written Language & Literacy 2(1): 1-44. DOI 10.1075/wll.2.1.02bir
tone_statements.quote: A fourth approach is possible when the tone occurring on a particular syllable is predictive of the tone pattern on the whole word. In Karang, an Adamawa language of Cameroon, tone on non word-initial syllables is never contrastive. Just the first syllable of each word is marked while later syllables are systematically unmarked (Ubels & Ubels 1986:6).
tone_statements.locator: preprint p. 8, section 3 'Spelling rules to minimise tone marking', paragraph 'A fourth approach'; journal pagination differs
tone_statements.summary: One second-hand passage in a pan-African tone-orthography survey: Karang tone is contrastive only on the word-initial syllable, which predicts the whole word's tone pattern; orthography marks tone on the first syllable only (after Ubels & Ubels 1986). No inventory, no Karang forms, no stress data.

tone_statements.citation: Ubels, Edward H. 1983. Mood and aspect in Karang. Studies in African Linguistics 14(1): 47-70. DOI 10.32473/sal.v14i1.107535
tone_statements.quote: Regardless of the CV pattern, every verb root has one tone. Two tone classes, mid and low, are established on the basis of the tone which occurs on the root in its most unmarked form, which is defined as the form occuring when the root functions as the main verb in a negated factive sentence. … The tone of the morpheme is marked as follows: high ('), low ('), rising (Y); mid tone is unmarked. … Rule 1 says that for non-factive mood add a high tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 49, sect. 1.1 'Phonology and morphology of the verb' and fn. 2; Rule 1 on p. 56, sect. 3.2.1

sources.citation: Ulfers, Robert Ernst (comp.). 2007. Dictionnaire karang - français. Yaoundé, Cameroun: SIL. 148 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 32270; file)
sources.note: Dictionary orthography guide: names high, mid, low tones and old-orthography rising marks; lexical minimal pairs (mí/mì, fál/fàl, ké/kè); grammatical tone (incompletive verb raised to high; subjunctive pronouns high). No count; rising written as level sequence (/bāá/ = bǎh). ~2,940 tone-marked forms.

tone.quote: ... exige seulement que le ton haut soit écrit sur certains mots (ton lexical). ... Le nouveau système d’écriture minimise l’utilisation de toutes les marques de tons bas ( ̀ ) et toutes les marques de tons montants ( ̌ ) qui étaient employées dans l’ancien système de 1980. ... Les actions non-accomplies en langue karang sont indiquées par un changement de prononciation de ton sur le verbe d’un ton bas ou moyen à un ton haut. ... Mais dans l’action non-accomplie ‘ Il viendra aujourd’hui.’ - Ke gí guri., ... Il est prononcé avec un ton haut.
tone.locator: p. 7, 'L’orthographe de marques de ton' / 'Comment marquer le ton lexical' / 'Comment marquer le ton grammatical'
tone.translation: ... [the new orthography] requires only that high tone be written on certain words (lexical tone). ... The new writing system minimises the use of all the low-tone marks ( ̀ ) and all the rising-tone marks ( ̌ ) that were used in the old 1980 system. ... Incompletive actions in Karang are indicated by a change of tone pronunciation on the verb from a low or mid tone to a high tone. ... But in the incompletive 'He will come today' - Ke gí guri. - ... It is pronounced with a high tone.

No count; rising written as level sequence (/bāá/ = bǎh). ~2,940 tone-marked forms.

sources.citation: Ulfers, Robert Ernst & David Ngang. 2000. A practical study of the orthography of compound words in the Karang language (ALCAM 352). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 37 pp. (SIL Cameroon archives 47547; file)
sources.note: Orthography-testing report, not a phonology: it presupposes tone (verbs in compounds carry an 'inflected high tone', ex. kɔ́r vs kɔr; a 1998 committee decision reduced tone marking) but gives no tone inventory or system; refers to Ulfers & Ngang 1998 on minimizing tone marking. Nothing on stress.

tone.quote: It was essential to know if these compounds needed to be written as whole words because the verbs in these compounds always carry the inflected high tone mark. If the were written as suchh, it might help the reader distinguish the compound from a verb phrase, as seen in examples 6 and 7 below. Example 6. Nzuk kɔ́r waka person guard(inflected) farm “farm guard” Example 7. Nzuk kɔr waka person guard farm “The person guarded the farm” However the in 1998 the Comité de Langue Karang adopted a new system of tone marking in which the above tone is no longer marked.
